title: From 2012 Gaza War to 2014 Gaza War
sub: Connection and background to 2014 Gaza War

markers.label: Gaza Strip
markers.description: After 2012, Hamas rebuilt rockets and attack tunnels while Israeli communities remained exposed.

slides.title: From 2012 Gaza War to 2014 Gaza War
slides.cap: Historical overview: From 2012 Gaza War to 2014 Gaza War
slides.body:
The 2012 ceasefire left Hamas in power and did not stop military rebuilding. The kidnapping and murder of three Israeli teenagers, West Bank arrests, reciprocal attacks, and renewed rocket fire produced another rapid escalation.

Israel aimed to stop sustained rocket attacks and destroy cross-border attack tunnels that threatened nearby Israeli communities.

This background is essential to understanding 2014 Gaza War: the conflict emerged from accumulated security failures, political choices, and unresolved disputes rather than from a single isolated incident. The recorded indicators, including 2012 Gaza War (previous conflict in this path) and 8 July-26 August 2014 (conflict period), help convey the episode's scale and the pressures facing decision-makers.

slides.title: Operation Protective Edge Begins
slides.cap: Historical overview: Operation Protective Edge Begins
slides.body:
Israel began airstrikes after intensified rocket fire from Gaza. Hamas launched rockets across much of Israel, while Iron Dome limited casualties in populated areas.

The 2014 campaign centered on two threats Israeli leaders could not ignore: long-range rocket fire and cross-border attack tunnels built to reach Israeli communities. The operation combined airstrikes, Iron Dome, and ground action against tunnel infrastructure.

slides.title: Zikim Sea Infiltration
slides.body:
Hamas naval commandos attempted to enter Israel near Zikim. Israeli forces stopped the raid, but it demonstrated Hamas's effort to bypass border defenses with specialized units.

slides.cap: Historical overview: Ground Operation Against Tunnels
slides.body:
Israel launched a ground operation after discovering cross-border tunnels used for attacks. Tunnel destruction became the central Israeli objective and brought intense combat in northern and eastern Gaza.

slides.title: Battle of Shuja'iyya
slides.body:
Israeli troops fought a major battle in a heavily fortified neighborhood used by Hamas forces. Thirteen Golani soldiers and many Palestinians were killed, illustrating the severe cost of urban combat.

slides.title: Rafah Attack and Hadar Goldin
slides.cap: Historical overview: Rafah Attack and Hadar Goldin
slides.body:
During a humanitarian ceasefire, Hamas fighters attacked Israeli troops near Rafah, killing two and taking the body of Lieutenant Hadar Goldin. The event triggered intense Israeli fire and became a lasting national issue.

markers.description: Egyptian mediation produced the open-ended ceasefire after weeks of fighting.

slides.title: Open-Ended Ceasefire
slides.body:
Egypt brokered an open-ended ceasefire after fifty days. Israel had destroyed many tunnels and degraded Hamas, but rocket threats and the political struggle over Gaza remained.

markers.description: The war centered on rockets and tunnels aimed at Israeli civilians and border communities.

slides.title: Conflict Summary: 2014 Gaza War
slides.cap: Historical overview: Conflict Summary: 2014 Gaza War
slides.body:
Israel destroyed many attack tunnels and reduced immediate rocket fire, but Hamas remained in control and both sides prepared for future conflict. The war caused major Israeli military losses and devastating Palestinian casualties and destruction.

Taken as a whole, 2014 Gaza War shows how battlefield achievements can alter the balance of power without necessarily producing a durable political settlement. The outcome must therefore be judged by the security conditions it created, the threats that survived, the human cost, and whether later leaders learned from the campaign.
